descriptionMd:
The maintenance desk joins connected switchboard sockets into shared cable families. Pia adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

links is a symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix. Union every connected pair, then produce the size of the component containing each vertex, in vertex order. Self-links do not change a component.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement cableFamiliesBossReceipt(links, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Union-find components. links is a symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix. Union every connected pair, then produce the size of the component containing each vertex, in vertex order. Self-links do not change a component. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The adjacency matrix is square and has at most 16 vertices; binary entries are 0 or 1, weighted entries are 0 through 13.

Target time O(V^2 alpha(V)); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.

links is a symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix. Union every connected pair, then produce the size of the component containing each vertex, in vertex order. Self-links do not change a component. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.
